notes: Perfect claim overlap (C7-C9, C41-C43) on synthetic lethality of double mutants. Both agree the genetic data is strong, though peer reviewers request additional electrophysiological characterization of rescued animals.

Perfect claim overlap (C10-C12, C77-C82) on additive genetic interactions for synaptic vesicle numbers. Both accept the data as strong, with peer reviewers requesting p-values for statistical clarity rather than questioning findings.

Perfect claim overlap (C83-C86) on vesicle size increase. Both evaluators question the biological significance and interpretation, with peer reviewers explicitly challenging whether size changes imply a direct role in size determination versus indirect disruption of endocytic fidelity.

Perfect claim overlap (C92-C99) on electrophysiological characterization. Both accept the data as strong and valid, with peer reviewers requesting p-values for clarity and noting that direct endocytosis assays were not performed (contextual comment, not challenge).

Perfect claim overlap (C124-C125, C136, C140) on AP2-independent endocytosis mechanisms. Both accept that double mutants retain ~30% vesicles and functional synapses, demonstrating alternative pathways exist.

High overlap (87.5%, C14, C72, C100-C102, C106, C108) on the core hemicomplex model. Both strongly support the conclusion that AP2 functions as two partially independent hemicomplexes, with peer reviewers requesting discussion of hemicomplex contribution in wild-type rather than challenging the model.

High overlap (85.7%, C13, C87, C89-C90, C137-C138) on large vesicle/vacuole accumulation. Both accept the ultrastructural observations as valid data, with peer reviewers suggesting contextual citations to similar phenotypes in other mutants.

Moderate overlap (62.5%, C48-C50, C52-C53) on cargo-specific endocytosis defects. LLM finds the differential cargo requirements well-documented and sufficient. Peer reviewers accept the data but suggest additional experiments with tyrosine-based motifs would significantly strengthen the hemicomplex model, indicating current evidence leaves some uncertainty.

Moderate overlap (50%, C58-C61, C64-C65, C67, C69, C71, C103-C104) on hemicomplex stability. Both accept the biochemical data showing partially stable hemicomplexes in single mutants as strong evidence, with peer reviewers requesting clarification about residual function for textual clarity.

Moderate overlap (50%, C75-C76) on synaptic protein accumulation in axons. LLM accepts this as functional evidence for trafficking defects. Peer reviewers explicitly challenge this interpretation, stating it is not possible at the light level to know whether altered axon/synapse ratios reflect recycling defects, requiring additional discussion of limitations.

Partial overlap (31.2%, C62-C63, C66, C68, C107) on reduced hemicomplex stability. Both accept the biochemical measurements showing reduced protein levels in single mutants, with peer reviewers seeking clarification about functional implications rather than questioning the data.

Minimal overlap (8.7%, C3-C4 only) on viability and partial function. LLM groups viability with tissue-specific rescue and functional distinctions (C35-C40). Peer review groups viability with molecular characterization and hemicomplex stability (C2, C5-C6, C58-C72). Both support overlapping claims but organize evidence differently.

Minimal overlap (4.3%, C2 only) on molecular characterization. LLM focuses on null allele identification (C2, C29-C34). Peer review groups C2 with viability, hemicomplex stability, and broader genetic findings (C3-C6, C58-C72). Both support C2 but embed it in different conceptual frameworks.

Minimal overlap (7.7%, C105 only) where LLM groups cargo-specificity with overall hemicomplex model (C14, C72, C100-C108) and finds it strongly supported. Peer review isolates cargo data (C48-C50, C52-C53, C105) and suggests additional experiments needed, indicating uncertainty about the full scope of the hemicomplex model.

Minimal overlap (4.2%, C72 only) where both support the hemicomplex conclusion but organize supporting evidence differently. LLM emphasizes converging genetic and functional evidence; peer review emphasizes molecular characterization and stability data.
